keyFindings.description: image_go reads `$source`, the row's Docker Hub upstream at its digest, for every library/golang row on every ci-images run, held or copied. The package holds the same digest, so the read can come from `$registry@$digest`. As written it puts an anonymous Docker Hub fetch back into a CI job on every run that selects ci_images (each pull request touching the three filter files, each merge group, each such push to main), which is the fault class this change removes, and makes ci-images.yaml:10-11's 'reads Docker Hub a few times a year' false. Fix: read the config from the package for a held row and from the upstream only before a copy (or from the package after the copy), and keep the prose true.

The mirror script decides which rows are library/golang with its own parser, stripping only Docker Hub hosts, while check-ci-images.sh's upstream_parts strips any host. A row such as mirror.gcr.io/library/golang:1.27.1-alpine counts as the Go row for rules 3 and 7 but gets claimed_go='' here, so the Go check skips it silently: the label-bytes mismatch this round set out to catch. Fix: one shared parser module both scripts import (PYTHONPATH=.github/scripts, as workflow_paths is), or rule 1 refusing a row whose upstream host is not Docker Hub; add a case.
The refusal says to write the digest golang:$claimed_go names, which drops the -alpine variant (golang:1.27.1 is the Debian image); name the row's own upstream instead.
Dead fixture lines left by the deleted tag read (:142-143, :204's tags append) and the harness prose describing upstream-tag reads (:8-9, :12-13, :116-117).
'every library/golang row' — a golang row whose upstream names a digest alone is skipped; say 'every tagged library/golang row'.
